recommendation: Keep the empty audit commit. Do not change Resource.id to FHIR.id under FHIR-44817; if FHIR-37861 or a later applied issue lands, handle case annotations and any additional explanatory comments under that issue's own decision.
issue_request: FHIR-44817 asked whether Patient.id/Resource.id should be treated in FHIRPath as System.String or FHIR.id. The Jira issue is Applied for R6 with resolution Not Persuasive with Modification, recording the underlying concern that Resource.id should carry FHIR id datatype constraints while not having primitive id/extension children.
initial_application: Commit 415c4e014bc12bc9f0724783f92d17f1e267bbe3 explicitly applied FHIR-44817 by adding Resource.id examples to source/fhirpath.html. Those examples state that Patient.id is System.String and that Patient.id is not FHIR.id.
additional_context: The authoritative Resource source defines Resource.id with type code http://hl7.org/fhirpath/System.String and structuredefinition-fhir-type value id. FHIR-25274 had already published the ElementDefinition guidance for this System.String plus fhir-type pattern. Later final issue FHIR-45989 resolved no-change and states that Resource.id is defined as System.String with FHIR type id: it behaves as a string with no extensions while its wire value is constrained by id datatype rules. FHIR-37861 proposes additional FHIRPath example case/comment cleanup but is not Applied/Published, so it was treated only as background.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current FHIRPath page and Resource StructureDefinition already express the reconciled rule for this issue family: Resource.id is represented as a FHIRPath System.String value constrained by FHIR id rules, not as a full FHIR.id primitive with id/extension children.
